## Natural history notes

A small leafcutter-family bee characterized by its entirely black body, compact build, and relatively dark, unmarked appearance compared with many more colorful megachilid bees. In Florida, Stelis ater is a rare Florida-associated cuckoo bee, with records including natural areas in north-central Florida and recognition as a conservation-relevant bee species in the state. Unlike pollen-collecting bees, it is cleptoparasitic: females lay eggs in the nests of other solitary bees, with Osmia chalybea documented as a host, and the developing Stelis larva uses the host nest’s provisions rather than building and provisioning its own nest.
